text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT AUTO-PAGE — latency SLO breach (p95) on /v1/generate in hosted-us-east. Auto-routing policy 'latency-fallback' triggered twice in last 2m. Runbook: https://internal/runbooks/latency-routing

ari_oncall: seeing pages, taking incident lead. Can someone post quick numbers?

bob_sre: p95 = 1.2s for the last 2m (normal ~360ms). Error rate stable (<0.1%), but we have rapid reroutes: routing decision timestamps: 1867890045, 1867890067, 1867890091. So ~20-30s flip interval.

cam_runtime: looking. Routing policy has switch_cooldown = 30s and latency_threshold = 700ms. Hysteresis is not enabled. Policy snippet:```yaml
policy: latency-fallback
rules:
  - metric: p95_latency
    threshold: 700ms
    switch_cooldown: 30s
    fallback: model-v2-quantized-us-east
```
This short cooldown + single threshold causes flip/flop when p95 hovers around threshold and we fall back to a variant that changes load shape.

dee_product: two paying customers reported client timeouts and retries in the last 3 minutes. Dee has their support tickets. Potentially 1-2 minute visible impact for them.

lee_support: attaching sample request traces: trace-id 0a1b2c -> long tail at runtime service, spilling into fallback variant which has KV cache cold misses. Also see many KV cache misses within 10s of a switchover.

ari_oncall: proposed immediate mitigations (live):
- Pause auto-routing or increase cooldown to stop thrash
- Force route to last-known-good variant for hosted-us-east while we stabilize
- Scale dedicated pool for hosted-us-east if capacity looks constrained
Which one can we do fastest?

bob_sre: we can pause auto-routing via console in ~30s. Forcing variant route is a single API call. Scaling dedicated pool needs a deploy/scale and may take 2-3min. Recommend pause routing + force variant, then scale.

cam_runtime: agreed. I'll patch the policy to disable auto-switches and set a longer cooldown. Executing:```bash
# disable auto switch
redwoodctl routing update --policy latency-fallback --set auto_enabled=false
# set cooldown to 300s as stopgap
redwoodctl routing update --policy latency-fallback --set switch_cooldown=300s
```
Applying...

cam_runtime: applied. API returned: {"status":"ok","policy":"latency-fallback","auto_enabled":false,"switch_cooldown":"300s"}

cam_runtime: forcing route to model-v2-stable-us-east now:```bash
redwoodctl route set --service /v1/generate --region us-east --model model-v2-stable-us-east --force
```
Command OK — new route pinned.

maya_infra: starting scale of dedicated pool (hosted-us-east) +2 instances. ETA ~2m.

incident-bot: page note — applied policy patch by cam_runtime.

bob_sre: metrics update: p95 dropped to ~480ms after pin and before infra scaling finished. Looks like thrash was main issue (cold fallback variant + cache misses).

lee_support: confirmed reduced client errors in the last minute from customers A and B. They still want postmortem and RCA.

ari_oncall: can we keep auto_enabled=false for now? We'll do a controlled rollout later. Also create a temp circuit-breaker so further auto switches require manual approval.

cam_runtime: will keep disabled. Adding circuit-breaker and hysteresis as follow-up. Planned policy change: switch_cooldown=300s, hysteresis=true, require_approval=true for cross-variant switches. Example planned snippet:```yaml
switch_cooldown: 5m
hysteresis: true
approval_required: true
failover_mode: graceful
```

maya_infra: scale complete. Dedicated pool instances +2. No instance errors.

bob_sre: current p95 steady ~420-500ms for 3 successive 1m windows. Good.

dee_product: sending customer update now: short incident, mitigation applied, next update in 60m.

ari_oncall: incident-> mitigated. We'll keep channel open for 30m and then move to postmortem. Action items:
- cam_runtime: post a PR to change routing defaults to include hysteresis and longer cooldown (urgent)
- bob_sre: run synthetic canary to validate fallback variant doesn't cause cold-cache spike
- lee_support: collate customer-facing timeline and tickets
- maya_infra: add capacity-monitoring alert to detect KV cache churn during switches

bob_sre: +1 on canary. Also recommend we tune the policy threshold to 800ms vs 700ms for this endpoint since p95 distribution is noisy at high concurrency.

cam_runtime: acknowledged. I'll open the PR and link here. PR: https://internal/code/routing/policies/PR-482

ari_oncall: thanks all. If p95 remains stable we'll close the channel in 30m. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: incident status -> mitigated. Severity: Sev3 (customer impact, limited). Auto-paging silenced for this policy until policy changes are deployed.

cam_runtime: follow-up notes for postmortem: root cause = aggressive auto-switch policy (short cooldown + no hysteresis) + fallback variant with cold KV cache that temporarily increased latency. Fix = policy defaults to include hysteresis, longer cooldown, and approval gating for cross-variant switches; add warmup for fallback model or route overlap to prevent cold misses.

ari_oncall: logging this as postmortem task. Closing in 30m unless new alerts.
